Wavelet-Based Techniques for Non-Integer-Order Optimal Control Problems

Abstract:

This thesis focuses on developing efficient and accurate numerical methods for a broad class of optimal control problems involving fractional, variable-order, and distributed-order operators. Particular attention is given to systems governed by integro-differential dynamics, multi-dimensional state and control variables, and the presence of time-delay effects. Such problems naturally arise in science and engineering, where memory, hereditary properties, and complex dynamical behaviors must be accurately modeled, yet their analytical solution is often intractable. The central idea of this work is the systematic use of fractional wavelet functions such as Euler, Chelyshkov, Legendre, Lucas, and Hermite wavelets together with newly constructed operational matrices for fractional integration, variable-order operators, and product terms. These tools transform complex fractional optimal control problems into finite-dimensional systems of algebraic equations, which are then solved efficiently using the Lagrange multiplier technique and Galerkin methods. This direct wavelet-based framework provides a unified and computationally effective strategy for dealing with problems involving linear-nonlinear dynamics and singular distributed-order operators. The thesis makes several significant contributions. First, it introduces novel operational matrices for fractional, variable-order, and distributed-order integrals in different wavelet families. Second, it extends the framework to multi-dimensional and time-delay settings, which are crucial for realistic modeling of physical and engineering processes. Third, it formulates and analyzes distributed-order optimal control problems and develops corresponding wavelet-based numerical schemes. For each class of problems, the existence and uniqueness of solutions, necessary and sufficient optimality conditions, rigorous convergence analysis, and error estimates are established, ensuring the theoretical reliability of the proposed methods. Numerical examples are presented in extensive detail to validate the proposed schemes. The numerical results are validated against available analytical or benchmark solutions, confirming the accuracy and reliability of the proposed method. These include benchmark test problems as well as examples motivated by real-world applications. The results confirm the high accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness of the developed schemes, while also demonstrating their superiority over existing techniques in the literature. Future work includes extending the proposed methods to stochastic systems, adaptive schemes, and large-scale real-time applications, as well as integrating wavelet-based neural networks with PINNs for high-dimensional fractional optimal control problems and real-world engineering applications, supported by rigorous theoretical analysis of existence, uniqueness, convergence, stability, and error estimates.
